title: The Escarpment of Mount Kessler
premise: Rafael Nakamura has spent seven years outrunning a past she buried under a new name, ferrying supplies up the Kessler River for the mining concession that owns the valley. When a geological survey team goes silent above the escarpment, her employer forces her to fly the search, and a storm landing strands her with the expedition's sole survivor, Dr. Imogen Vale, who knows what Rafael's real name was. Together they descend the flooded river in a leaking boat while the monsoon closes in and the survey's findings — evidence the concession will kill to bury — make them fugitives on their own route home. Rafael ends the journey by choosing to testify under her true name, trading her anonymity for the found family that survived the river with her.
about_author: Jude Whitlock is the pen name of a former bush mechanic who spent a decade working remote airstrips across three continents before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people whose pasts are heavier than their cargo.

chapters.title: Fuel, Rumors, Rain
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A routine supply run into Kessler Landing introduces the valley's rhythms: the concession's tightening grip, the monsoon building over the escarpment, and rumors that the survey team upstream has gone quiet. Rafael deflects a radio operator's friendly questions about where she came from. Emotional beat: competent loneliness — she trusts the wilderness more than people.

chapters.title: The Silence Above the Falls
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The concession's manager, Brandt, orders her to fly the escarpment plateau and check on the survey camp despite weather closing in. She finds the camp wrecked, radios smashed, one grave dug too shallow, and no sign of the geologists. On takeoff through a squall she clips trees and crash-lands on a gravel bar downstream. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Imogen Vale, the survey's botanist, drags the injured pilot out of the wrecked plane and reveals fragments of what happened: the team found something in the escarpment strata, and men from the concession arrived the same night. She is evasive about how she alone escaped. Emotional beat: wary mutual dependence between two women both hiding things.

chapters.title: Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With the plane unflyable and the road washed out, they salvage the survey's aluminum boat, patching it with sealant and hope. The first day downriver establishes their fragile system — bailing shifts, rationed fuel, Imogen's maps against Rafael's river knowledge. At night Rafael catches Imogen studying her, and lies badly about her name. Emotional beat: uneasy truce.

chapters.title: What the Strata Kept
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Sheltering in an abandoned mission station, Imogen shows Rafael the samples: mineral signatures that prove the concession falsified its environmental filings, enough to void every permit downstream. She admits the team voted to go public, and that the 'accident' followed. Rafael recognizes Brandt's signature on the permits. Emotional beat: the stakes shift from survival to witness.

chapters.title: The Man from Downriver
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A concession patrol boat overtakes them at a rapids portage; its lead man, Okafor, once flew co-pilot with Rafael and knows her old callsign. He offers them passage — and quietly warns them Brandt has reported the plane stolen and Rafael as a suspect. They refuse the ride; he lets them go, but takes Imogen's sample case at gunpoint. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening the bond.

chapters.title: Monsoon
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The storm hits in earnest. The patched seam splits in white water; they lose most of their supplies and beach on a ledge below the escarpment wall, where Imogen breaks her wrist hauling Rafael from the current. Trapped for two days, they finally trade truths: Rafael's real name, the accident she fled, why she vanished. Emotional beat: confession as survival — the price of being known.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Road
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Rather than run the worst rapids, they climb the old survey track along the escarpment face toward the concession's upper airstrip, Imogen navigating on a broken wrist while Rafael hauls them both. They discover the missing geologists' final cache — duplicate samples and a signed affidavit hidden before the attack. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Permits Expire
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. They reach the airstrip as Brandt's men arrive to destroy the cache ahead of the permit deadline. In a night confrontation among the hangars, Okafor switches sides, having read the file on Rafael's 'stolen' plane and understood who the thief really was. Rafael flies the battered survey plane out through the storm's last edge with Imogen and the evidence aboard. Emotional beat: climax — skill, luck, and chosen loyalty against the clock.

chapters.title: Her True Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Weeks later, in the provincial capital, Rafael signs her testimony using the name she buried, watched by Imogen and Okafor. The permits are suspended; the concession's filings unravel. She takes a contract flying for the resettled survey region — not fleeing this time but staying. Emotional beat: resolution — identity reclaimed not as exposure but as arrival, with family she chose.
